judgements.justification: B's area chair gave a spotlight on 7, 6, 7, 7 with no reviewer above 7 or arguing for the tier and no reason stated, so the tier rests on the area chair's own unexplained call.
No reviewer or area chair rested a recommendation on impact beyond video instance segmentation and tracking; TiXB's 'very excited about the prospects' is about the method's own setting.
After a near-identical rebuttal, B's Reviewer_NPPQ (6 to 7) and Reviewer_HvVc (to 7) raised, while no A score moved.
Thin reviews sit on both sides (A: Reviewer_nMFp, Reviewer_h7Rc; B: Reviewer_NPPQ), and A's two most careful reviews (x3ez, q7JA) drove its reject, so scrutiny is not lopsided.

Only A found that PCAN is not faster than non-local attention and gains 0.5-0.6 AP, and only A asked for MAST and tuning on the reporting split; both efficiency and related work are in A's reasons for reject.
Both saw the same memory saving, best online results, missing prototype count, missing details, no KITTI-MOTS and modest novelty; A read them as a reject, B as a spotlight.
No score in either committee moved on other reviewers' views; B's raises cite the rebuttal and A's scores never moved.
Reviewer_nMFp's 6 on four one-line strengths is a thin review, not a rating that contradicts a stated verdict; no other rating clashes with its text.
NPPQ admitted not being an MOTS expert but rated 7 at confidence 4, not a borderline default; no committee's mean was held near threshold by declared uncertainty.
Neither area chair adopted a single outlying reviewer's verdict; neither committee had an outlier.
The verbal assessments differ: A's reviewers called it a 'pure application paper' with a 'trivial' gain, while B's saw 'a big step', so this is not one verdict placed at different scores.

B's meta-review leads with 'All four reviewers recommend acceptance' and no B rating exceeds 7, but A's scores are lower (mean 5.25, maximum 6), so the definition's comparison with the other committee fails.
B's Reviewer_HvVc called the paper 'badly written' with 'many crucial details missing' and raised to accept on promised revisions to the text and figures.
B's meta-review carries the presentation weakness and TiXB's prototype ablation forward, and A's lists its reviewers' concerns; neither drops its reviewers' weaknesses.
A's Reviewer_h7Rc called YouTube-VIS a VOS dataset, which Section 4.1 refutes, and B's Reviewer_NPPQ called the prototype attention new though Section 2 cites EM-based prototype attention [19].
The damaging admission (PCAN 63.2 vs 61.8 ms per frame) went to A, which stayed at reject, so it did not leave that committee higher than its information supported.
A's area chair cites non-public concerns, but low novelty and self-supervised work were raised in the reviews and answered in the rebuttal; no post-response objection or score cut is on record.
The committees' scores are far apart (means 5.25 and 6.75), not near-identical profiles split by tier cut-offs.
A's best-informed reviewer, Reviewer_x3ez (confidence 5), rated 5 and A's area chair followed that side; B's confidences are all 4.

B's main concerns (prototype count, missing details, KITTI-MOTS) were closed by new tables, while A's central objections (application paper without insight, no speed gain, 0.5-0.6 AP over non-local attention) no response could remove.
Neither committee had an outlying score; A's 6 is one point from its 5s and B's 6 one point from its 7s.
No reviewer stood apart from their committee; A's silence after the rebuttal was by three of four reviewers, not by an outlier.
Neither committee had a detractor set aside as unreliable.
No reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit.

added.name: Meta-review misstated the reviewers' positions or rebuttal
added.definition: One committee's meta-review misreported the record it summarised, such as the reviewers' final positions or which concerns the authors' response had already answered, and that committee's recommendation rested on the inaccurate account.
added.justification: R14 covers a meta-review that drops its reviewers' weaknesses and R15 a wrong claim about the paper's results; neither covers an area chair misreporting the reviewers' stance or the rebuttal's content against the paper.

added.name: One committee's reviewers left the rebuttal unanswered
added.definition: Most of one committee's reviewers never replied to the authors' response or joined the public discussion, so scores set before a response that answered their points stood unrevised, while the other committee's reviewers engaged with the response and revised.
added.justification: R03 records that the response persuaded one committee and not the other, which reads as a reasoned judgement; R22 covers silence by an outlying reviewer only. Neither names silence by most of a committee as the mechanism.

reasoning: The two committees saw the same strengths and gaps and weighed them differently (R06). B's reviewers engaged with a rebuttal that closed their fixable gaps and two raised, one on promised revisions (R03, R13, R20); A's three silent reviewers and x3ez's unmoved 5 left its scores where they were, a mechanism of non-engagement that no reason named, so I added R26. Only A probed runtime and related work (R05). Each side held a factual misreading (R15). A's meta-review called all reviewers negative and listed answered concerns, which R14 and R15 do not cover, so I added R25. B's spotlight on no rating above 7 is the area chair's unexplained call (R01); R12 fails its comparative clause because A's scores are lower.
